messages:
alex: Heads-up — canary-3 (eu-west) showed a reconnect spike at ~11:03 and our streaming p95 latency SLO was breached for ~6m. Pattern looks like: client reconnect -> routing falls back to 'dedicated-burst' -> immediate reconnect backoff -> client retries and sometimes gets stitched to both pools. Not sure if it's a routing policy bug or a backoff edge-case.

maria: Ugh. Any evidence of duplicate billing or token churn?

alex: Two things: telemetry shows duplicated route_ids for some connection ids, and billing peeked for that tenant for the same window. Attaching a small snippet from the proxy logs:

alex: ```
[11:03:02] conn=abc123 route=primary lease=60s -> upstream 10.1.2.3
[11:03:04] conn=abc123 AUTH ERROR -> client reconnect
[11:03:05] conn=abc123 route=fallback dedicated-burst lease=30s
[11:03:05] conn=abc123 kvcache=miss prefix=\"\"
[11:03:06] conn=abc123 route=primary lease=60s (resume success)
```

jon: That log looks like the proxy is re-associating the same conn id with two different routes within <1s. If the resume flows cause the client to replay tokens to both backends, we could be charging twice. Is the resume idempotency check scoped to route or to global conn id?

lee: Last I checked, resume idempotency is only global per connection id, but routing fallbacks mutate the backend header before resume validation. So resume check might be bypassed if route header differs.

maria: Can we confirm with a quick query? Something like: 
```
select count(*) by tenant, route_id from sse_events where event in ('resume','connect') and ts between 3412345600 and 3412345800
```
Also check duplicate resume ids within 5s.

jon: Running now — small sample matches: tenant=acme route=primary 45, route=d edicated-burst 43, but 28 resume_ids appear on both routes. That's the smoking gun.

ops-bot: deploy: rollout/eng-platform/route-fallback-2026-03-20 started by lee at 11:12 (canary -> 10%).

alex: Perfect — thank you. So root cause hypothesis: sticky-routing lease + immediate fallback -> resume id seen by new backend with different route header -> resume idempotency check doesn't de-duplicate because route header changed. Leads to duplicate processing and billing.

lee: Two-pronged fix suggested: (1) Make resume idempotency canonicalize scope to connection UUID only (ignore route header), (2) Add a short debounce window before routing fallback upgrades to another pool (like 200-500ms) to prevent flip-flop.

maria: Also console UX issue: current streaming request view only shows final route. We need to surface the fallback chain (primary -> attempted fallback -> final) so customers and SREs can see why a request ended up on dedicated-burst. Filing a console-ticket. @console-team can we add a breadcrumb view with route transitions for streaming sessions?

console-team: Noted — can mock a minimal breadcrumb in the next sprint. Two questions: do we have an event model with route transitions? If not, we need to emit a `route_transition` event per connection.

jon: We can emit an event. Small schema: `{conn_id, prev_route, next_route, reason, ts}`. Should be cheap. Telemetry retention can be short (7d) for these breadcrumbs.

alex: Agreed. Also for debugging, please add a flag to the console to show last 1m of raw proxy logs for the conn_id (masking tokens). That would have saved us 10m of triage.

lee: Priority: hotfix for resume idempotency today (canary asap). Debounce policy and console telemetry next week. Ops: throttle further canary expansion until we confirm no double-charge.

maria: For billing reconciliation, run a query to surface sessions with same resume_id and overlapping token counts across different routes and produce an offset report. I'll take that.

jon: I can PR the resume-id fix — change the check from `(resume_id, route)` -> `(resume_id)` and add a unit test simulating route flip. Will open in ~15m.

ops-bot: alert: billing-surge detected for tenant acme at 11:04 — alerted 2 engineers.

alex: Thanks everyone. Action items: jon (resume-id hotfix PR + canary), lee (hold canary expansion + add debounce config), console-team (breadcrumb event + UI mock), maria (billing reconciliation query). Tagging @sre for visibility.

lee: I'll patch config to set fallback-debounce=300ms in canary and pause expansion until we see 30m of stable metrics.

alex: Will follow up with a short postmortem doc once we have the reconciliation numbers. :thumbsup:
